reasons: The rule is kind 'missing', and Section 14.6 is a usable, mutual insurance covenant (product liability included, coverage for the whole clinical/commercial period, evidence on request, notice of cancellation from RevMed, and no cap on indemnification), so the 'no insurance clause' trigger is correctly not fired.

Walk-away territory is not engaged: RevMed is a research/development collaborator, not a data processor or on-premises services vendor, so the CGL/E&O/cyber stack is not the operative benchmark; the clause is fairly characterized as meeting the rule's intent at fallback level for this deal type.

Absent dollar thresholds and the missing one-year tail are correctly noted in the rationale as sub-preferred sub-elements rather than escalated to a deviation, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were produced; the rendered paragraph is identical to the original and the deterministic check ('insurance obligation present') supports the conclusion.
Features favoring our party (Sanofi-only self-insurance option, one-way cancellation-notice obligation on RevMed) were properly not flagged.
